Associated Social Effects
Changes resulting from coal development will have both disruptive and stabilizing influences on the people and the social structure of the community. The desirability of the changes associated with the urbanizing society would, to a large degree, be evaluated by subjective means based largely on the biases of the interpreter. The lower level of development (AF-1) would in itself cause relatively little social disruption, since it would require practically no relocation of local people and only a minor influx of outside employees. Of course, continuing social change is expected with or without development, and any change will be accompanied by some degree of socio-psychological trauma. Usually, ordinary evolutionary changes are not expected to seriously overload present institutions.
At the projected higher level of development (AF-2) however, significant accelerated social change must be anticipated. The Indian culture will be put under pressure to change, and as income levels rise, other socio-psychological changes are anticipated. There will be a tendency for increasingly acute social situations such as alcoholism and emotional disturbances, as well as some breakdown in the primary social bonds of the family and traditional community.
Community Identity - and cohesiveness will be severely tested as new residents, facilities, and institutions make their influence felt. If a community grows at a highly accelerated rate and dominant leadership roles shift, the community may take on characteristics which are distasteful to many residents.
